advances: Exact auxiliary continuous cap optimization at a prescribed weighted centroid. The charge includes one copy of the added measure; no mixed-integer allocation or center selection is asserted.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Work in volume units $|B|=1$. Move the cap boundary parallel to itself to pass through $g$; this can only decrease both charged masses. Let $X$ be the linear coordinate in the cap direction, $U(t)=|B\cap\{X\ge t\}|$, and $s=U(X(g))$. The centroid is interior because the density is at least one on the full-dimensional $B$, so $0<s<1$. Hyperplanes are null, and every open subinterval of the projection interval meets the projection of $\operatorname{int} B$ and has a preimage of positive volume. Hence $U$ is continuous and strictly decreasing on the projection interval, with endpoint values $1,0$, and $U(X)$ is uniform on $[0,1]$ under volume on $B$. The image of $\eta$ under $U(X)$ has density $h\in[0,1]$, integral $\alpha$, and mass $r=\eta(H)$ on $[0,s]$. This implies all the displayed linear constraints.

The $d$-th volume root in the Brunn–Minkowski statement recorded in 03f650d1c4f1b86d applies to the nonempty compact convex caps of $B$; their Minkowski interpolation lies in the cap at the interpolated threshold. Thus $U^{1/d}$ is concave on the projection interval, including its endpoints. Jensen with the probability measure $(\mathbf 1_B\,dx+k\eta)/(1+k\alpha)$ gives
$$
(1+k\alpha)s^{1/d}\ge\int_0^1 t^{1/d}(1+kh(t))\,dt.
$$
On each of $[0,s]$ and $[s,1]$, the indicator of the leftmost interval of the prescribed mass minimizes the integral against the increasing function $t^{1/d}$. To see this, subtract that indicator from $h$ and subtract the cutoff value from the integrand; the resulting product is pointwise nonnegative and the subtraction of a constant changes no integral. Integrating those two intervals and multiplying by $q$ proves the scalar inequality.

The scalar set is compact, with $s=0$ infeasible and $(s,r)=(1,\alpha)$ strictly feasible in the last inequality: its slack is $q-1+k\alpha(q-\alpha^{1/d})>0$. If a minimizer had strict slack, lower both $s,r$ by the same small amount when $r>0$, or lower only $s$ when $r=0$. The linear constraints persist (in the first case $s-r$ is fixed); continuity preserves slack. This strictly reduces the objective. Thus every minimizer has equality, and $s=1$, which forces $r=\alpha$, is excluded. In a simplex of volume one take $X$ to be a vertex barycentric coordinate. Then $U(X)=(1-X)^d$, so the Jensen step is an identity; choose the two bands for $\eta$. The scalar equality puts the centroid at $X=1-s^{1/d}$, and the through-cap has masses exactly $s,r$. At $\alpha=0$ one has $r=0$ and equality gives $s=q^{-d}$; at $\alpha=1$ one has $r=s$ and equality gives the same $s$.

For fixed $r$, the left-minus-right slack at $s=0$ is negative. For $s>0$ its derivative is
$$
q(q-1)(1+k\alpha)s^{q-2}-kq\bigl[(s+\alpha-r)^{q-1}-s^{q-1}\bigr]
\ \ge\ q(q-1)(1+kr)s^{q-2}>0,
$$
using concavity of the power $q-1\in(0,1]$. The lower derivative bound has divergent integral up to infinity, so there is exactly one positive root. The least allowed $s$ for each $r$ is then $\max\{r,t(r)\}$, provided it meets the upper bound $1-\alpha+r\le1$.
statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, $B\subset\mathbb R^d$ a compact convex body of positive $d$-volume, $0\le\eta\le\mathbf 1_B\,dx$, and $\alpha=\eta(B)/|B|$. Let $g$ be the centroid of $\mathbf 1_B\,dx+k\eta$. For a closed halfspace $H$ containing $g$, write $v=(|B\cap H|+\eta(H))/|B|$, $q=1+1/d$, and $\gamma_d=q^{-d}$. For real $k\ge1$ and fixed $\alpha\in[0,1]$, the sharp infimum of $v$ over $B,\eta,H$ is the attained minimum of $s+r$ under
$$
0\le s\le1,\quad 0\le r\le\min(\alpha,s),\quad s+\alpha-r\le1,\qquad
q(1+k\alpha)s^{q-1}\ge1+k r^q+k(s+\alpha-r)^q-k s^q.
$$
Every minimizing pair has $0<s<1$ and equality in the last constraint. A simplex with $\eta$ the volume restricted to its upper-tail quantile bands $[0,r]\cup[s,s+\alpha-r]$ attains every such pair. The endpoint optima at $\alpha=0,1$ are $\gamma_d,2\gamma_d$. Equivalently, for $r\in[0,\alpha]$ let $t(r)$ be the unique positive root in $s$ of the last constraint taken at equality, ignoring the other constraints. Minimize $r+\max\{r,t(r)\}$ over those $r$ with $\max\{r,t(r)\}\le1-\alpha+r$.
title: The sharp fixed-mass one-copy source cost
